chunks: One of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Bishr, from Mūsā ibn Qādim, from Sulaymān, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.

He said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, is greater, mightier, more majestic, and more exalted than to be wronged. But He joined us with Himself, so He made our being wronged His being wronged, and our wilayah His wilayah, where He says:
Your wali is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe.
Meaning the Imams from us. Then he said in another place:
And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.
Then he mentioned something similar to that.

key_terms.أَنْفُسَهُمْ: Themselves; indicating that the ultimate consequence of oppression returns to the oppressors themselves.
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ: The Imams; identified in the narration as those intended in the verse.
key_terms.خَلَطَنَا: He joined us with Himself; meaning He connected their cause and standing to His own.
key_terms.ظَلَمُونَا: They wronged Us; interpreted here as referring to wrongdoing against those whose cause Allah has joined to His own.
key_terms.ظُلْمَنَا: Our oppression; the ظلم committed against the Imams عليهم السلام.
key_terms.وَلَايَتَنَا: Our wilayah; the divinely appointed authority and guardianship of the Imams عليهم السلام.
key_terms.يَظْلِمُونَ: They commit ظلم; they act unjustly against themselves through their rejection and oppression.

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the verse “And they did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves”?
ai.summary: This narration explains that Allah, exalted above all deficiency, cannot literally be subject to injustice. Rather, He has connected the oppression of the Imams عليهم السلام and their wilayah to Himself, so violating their rights is described in the Qur’anic language as wrongdoing against Allah. The report therefore presents a theological and tafsir-based affirmation of the rank and authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
